::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Decr 21st 1897  
**Manuscript:** MS Girton College Cambridge, Yonge VII 5
:::

My dear [Canon Warburton](people/person_1466.qmd) 
Would it be asking too much of your kindness to ask you to glance over this paper and see whether it is an advisable one to have in [Mothers in Council](organizations/other_82.qmd).  I do not know whether you have heard of the [Mother's Union](organizations/other_31.qmd), started by [Mrs G Sumner](people/person_1381.qmd) (the wife of the [Bishop of Guildford](people/person_1382.qmd)) at first for poor women, to rouse them to some heed to the training of their children but it gradually spread to ladies &c. and indeed quite as much counsel seems to be needed by them as by cottage women.

‘The need of an ‘organ’ was soon felt, and <u>faute de mieux</u>, I have had to edit the quarterly ‘Mothers in Council’ of which I send a specimen since we are told that Mothers are afraid to teach their children Scripture from what they gather of the ‘Higher Criticism[‘].

I am afraid the subject must be opened but I am very anxious to do it in the right way

Yours very sincerely
C M Yonge
